name: Japan other
meta: Experiences, shopping and day trips that are not tied to one area.

must.line: A pillowy konbini egg salad sandwich, crusts off, better than it has any right to be.
Famichiki or Karaage-kun from the hot case by the till, the perfect late night snack.
Stone-ground green tea, whisked frothy and bitter-sweet, or in parfaits and ice cream.
Delicate seasonal sweets of bean paste and rice, made to be eaten with matcha.
Try a flight of small pours, dry to fruity, then buy the bottle you liked best.
Buy a bottle to take home: Japanese labels cost less here, if you can find them.

items.one: Egg sando, onigiri and fried chicken
items.fits: Any morning, or Tue 27 breakfast before the 06:22 walk to Shimbashi. There is a konbini on every block.

items.one: Department store food halls, Ginza best
items.fits: Sun 25 while you shop Mitsukoshi and Matsuya, for a tasting lap or a picnic dinner in the room. Mon 26 for gifts to take home.

items.one: Uji matcha parfaits on Ginza Six 4F
items.fits: Sun 25 afternoon break in Ginza Six, before the rooftop garden. Go before 15:00 or after 18:00 to dodge the queue.

items.one: Imperial wagashi and matcha in Ginza 7-chōme
items.fits: Sun 25 afternoon, open on your dates. A calmer, more traditional alternative to the matcha parfait.

items.one: Sake tasting bar inside Tokyo Station
items.fits: Sat 24 as you come off the Shinkansen at 14:15, before leaving the gates, if you have energy for a quick glass. Or Sun 25 at Tokyo Station with a platform ticket.

items.one: Sumo show with dinner in Ginza
items.fits: Sun 25 at 17:00: Hirakuza Ginza, 1-9-13 Ginza, a daily 17:00 show with a kaiseki dinner, from ¥17,000 each on Klook. Or Mon 26 at 11:00 at Tokyo Sumo Club in Tokyo Tower, straight after teamLab.

items.one: Old Ginza public bath, five minutes away
items.fits: Mon 26 at about 18:00, after Asakusa and before the Shimbashi dinner. Closed Sundays.
Any Shibuya evening at #C-pla, or Sun 25 at #C-pla premium in Ginza. Bring ¥100 coins.
Sun 25 in Ginza while Chūō-dōri is car-free. Passports for tax-free.

items.one: Flagship 100 yen shop, souvenirs and snacks
items.fits: Sun 25 in Ginza, same building as Loft. Good for cheap gifts and an extra bag.
Sun 25 in Ginza, same building as Daiso. Loft's beauty floor has a tester bar.
Sun 25 on the walk from Tokyo International Forum into Ginza, or Mon 26 evening for whisky to fly home. Tax-free.
Any shopping day. Carry your passport, not a copy, and keep sealed bags sealed until you are out of Japan.

items.one: Real onsen baths at Tokyo Dome City
items.fits: A wet evening, Sun 25 or Mon 26: Marunouchi line direct from Ginza to Kōrakuen, about 12 minutes. Cheaper after 19:00.

items.one: Lost in Translation karaoke rooms, Shibuya
items.fits: A late night in Shibuya, Sat 17 or Mon 19 after Shinjuku. Close to the hotel in Udagawachō.

items.one: Photo sticker booths, open all night
items.fits: Any Shibuya evening, a minute off Center-gai and close to the hotel. Do it together: couples are fine.

items.one: Onsen, Lake Ashi and Fuji views
items.fits: Not in the plan. A whole day from Shibuya via Shinjuku, so only if you drop Kamakura and Yokohama.
Not in the plan. Tōbu trains leave from Asakusa, so it would replace the Mon 26 Asakusa day.

notes: No sumo tournament runs on your dates, so a show is the way to see it. Hirakuza Ginza refunds only 50% within 21 days and nothing within 7 days, so decide this week. Spa LaQua refuses entry with tattoos. Japan's tax-free system changes on 1 November 2026: everything you buy in October uses the current tax-off-at-the-till system. Kakigōri is a summer dish and mostly off menus by late October, so it is left out.
